name: AMM linearised-stability criterion for validity of semiclassical gravity

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0209075 v1 (21 Sep 2002), Anderson, Molina-Paris & Mottola, 'Linear Response, Validity of Semi-Classical Gravity, and the Stability of Flat Space' (LA-UR-02-5809); PRD 67, 024026 (2003) per the owner (journal ref not re-read here). Abstract p.1; criterion Sec. III p.10; derivation of (3.4) pp.8-9; restatement Sec. V p.13.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(gr-qc/0209075) this stage, pages 1,4,5,8,9,10,13,14 of the v1 text layer; cross-checked against the cached alphaXiv text layer d67/amm_0209075.txt (the file the re-derivation searches). Appendix B and the bibliography not read (not needed for the criterion).

published_statement: Sec. III, p.10: 'We now state our stability criterion for the semi-classical approximation. A necessary condition for the validity of the large N semi-classical equations of motion (2.9) is that the linear response equations (3.4) should have no solutions with finite non-singular initial data for which any linearized gauge invariant scalar quantity grows without bound. Such a quantity must be constructed only from the linearized metric perturbation h_ab and its derivatives, and it must be invariant under allowed gauge transformations of the kind described by eq. (3.11).' Abstract: 'solutions to the semi-classical Einstein equations should be stable to linearized perturbations, in the sense that no gauge invariant perturbation should become unbounded in time.' Sec. V, p.13: 'If, for a given state and background geometry that solves the semi-classical equations, one or more solutions to the linear response equations experience unbounded growth in a gauge invariant sense, then the semi-classical approximation is not valid for that particular geometry, at least not for that particular state. Clearly this is a necessary, though perhaps not a sufficient condition for the validity of the approximation.'
published_hypotheses: P-H1 (p.8) the linear response equation is obtained by expanding the CTP effective action 'around a given semi-classical geometry g_ab that solves eq. (2.9)'; 'the first variation vanishes by (2.9)'; (p.9) the retarded correlator 'is evaluated in the background geometry of the leading order solution of the semi-classical equations (2.9)'

P-H2 large-N: N non-interacting (free) quantum scalar fields of arbitrary mass and curvature coupling are the only matter; (2.9) is the large-N, RG-improved one-loop equation from the action (2.7) (pp.5-6)
P-H3 an in-state |in> (CTP in-in formalism); the verdict is state-specific ('at least not for that particular state', p.13)
P-H4 renormalised Lambda, G_N, alpha, beta in (2.7)/(2.9); (3.4) needs no counterterms beyond those of (2.9)
P-H5 perturbations have finite non-singular initial data
P-H6 the growing quantity is a SCALAR, built ONLY from h_ab and its derivatives, invariant under allowed gauge transformations (3.11)

P-H7 allowed gauge transformations: (3.11) for any X^a, EXCLUDING singular gauge transformations in the initial data, and excluding any (3.11) under which the action (2.7) is not invariant (boundary/surface terms) (pp.9-10)
P-H8 status: NECESSARY condition; sufficiency explicitly left open ('perhaps not a sufficient', p.13)

ADDED SCOPE -- the criterion is applied 'IN THE CLASSICAL RADIAL SECTOR: YES, AND IT RETURNS STABLE' (linstab.py:32-33) and D26 is labelled 'LINEARISED STABILITY (AMM). Classical radial sector ...: THEOREM' (D26_CLAIM linstab.py:357-361; the D26 row linstab.py:229-237; carried into specthm.py:1097-1113 R8 and ledger.py:720-725). B (sympy): for ARBITRARY X^a(t,x,y,z) the linearised Riemann tensor of the pure-gauge h_ab = d_aX_b + d_bX_a vanishes in all 256 components, while X_0 = t^2 gives h_00 = 4t -> infinity: component growth is gauge artefact, so AMM's gauge-invariant-scalar restriction is load-bearing (the criterion is well posed only with it). C (sympy): toy x'' = -x linearised about the non-solution x0 = -(t/2)sin t carries residual r = cos t; zero-data response t sin(t)/2 is unbounded although every homogeneous solution is bounded -- a boundedness verdict off-solution is not a property of the dynamics, which is why AMM's H1 (and the tree's refusal on it) matters. D (z3): Valid->NoGrowth entails Growth->not Valid (unsat), does not entail NoGrowth->Valid (sat countermodel), and with NoGrowth undetermined both Valid and not-Valid are consistent -- the tree's NOT EVALUABLE is the correct logical status. later_literature.ref: Hu, Roura & Verdaguer, 'Induced quantum metric fluctuations and the validity of semiclassical gravity', gr-qc/0402029 (2004; PRD 70, 044002)
later_literature.what: Reads AMM's criterion as the stability of the EXPECTATION VALUE of the quantised metric perturbation (Sec. IV.B, p.9) and argues it 'should be generalized': the n-point (from n=2) correlation functions of h_ab must also stay bounded, including INDUCED fluctuations driven by the noise kernel, which cannot be retrieved from the linearised semiclassical equation (only from the Einstein-Langevin equation). Also (p.8) questions how AMM's discard of Planck-scale Fourier modes generalises to time-dependent backgrounds. Confirms AMM's necessary-not-sufficient status by argument; does not refute the criterion. Their own criterion also finds Minkowski stable (abstract). For the tree: a stronger criterion needs MORE (noise kernel on a solution of (2.9)), so the semiclassical refusal (H1 unestablished) is unchanged.

later_literature.what: The criterion's programme continued by one of its authors in a solvable 1+1 QED model; the abstract says validity there involves the impact of quantum fluctuations. Not read beyond the discover_papers abstract.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this item: the criterion is a DEFINITION with no numerical input (data_at_publication), so no later measurement can move it -- evidence AGAINST 'lacked data' here. What AMM lacked in 2002 was theory, not data: the stochastic-gravity treatment of induced metric fluctuations, published two years later (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer 2004), which argues the criterion is incomplete (necessary only). AMM had anticipated exactly that ('perhaps not a sufficient', p.13), so the later work extends rather than corrects. Having it does not change the tree's conclusion: the tree uses AMM only (i) as a necessary condition and (ii) to refuse a semiclassical verdict because no demand configuration is shown to solve (2.9) (H1); a stronger criterion needs the same solution plus the noise kernel, so the refusal stands and becomes harder, not easier, to lift. The only change the source forces on the tree is scope: the classical radial theorem is not an evaluation of AMM's criterion.
grade_evidence: The published criterion stands as stated, read at source: every string the owner quotes is verbatim (re-derivation A, 4/4), page III p.10 is correct, and the precondition the tree's refusal rests on (H1: the background must solve (2.9)) is stated at source even more directly than the owner quotes (p.8 'that solves eq. (2.9)'; p.13). No datum exists to move it (definition), the z3 check confirms the tree's NOT-EVALUABLE is the right logical status for a necessary condition, and the later literature (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer 2004) extends it without refuting it. The grade is NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree's USE is wider than the source's class and drops two clauses: (1) the h_ab-only clause of P-H6 and the singular-gauge exclusion of P-H7 are carried nowhere in linstab.py (shown by search); (2) the AMM label is put on a classical Israel-shell radial stability theorem (linstab.py:32-33, 357-361; specthm R8), while AMM's criterion is defined on (3.4), the linearisation of (2.9) with N free quantum scalars as the only matter -- a classical barotropic shell is outside that class. Neither drift moves the tree's D26 semiclassical refusal (D26 OPEN), and neither is an error in AMM. The canonical entry's 'not sufficient' strengthens AMM's 'perhaps not a sufficient' (p.13); the owner does not make that claim.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner either (a) relabels the classical radial sector as classical linear stability NOT evaluated under AMM's criterion and carries the h_ab-only and singular-gauge clauses, or (b) shows that (3.4) extended by classical shell matter reduces, at hbar -> 0 under P1-P4, to stability.py's shell equations and that R(tau) is a gauge-invariant scalar built only from h_ab (plausible under Birkhoff, not shown here). To WRONG: only a computed contradiction inside AMM's own setting (e.g. a pure-gauge mode that passes AMM's allowed-gauge rule yet makes a gauge-invariant h_ab-scalar grow) -- none is known or shown. To OPEN: none -- the source is read and the checkable parts are checked.
